title: Eiffel Tower Closes as Nationwide Strike and Protests Hit France
dek: Unions called a nationwide strike on Thursday that disrupted public transport and closed the Eiffel Tower. The Louvre limited visitor access and Versailles may close.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Eiffel Tower in Paris (file photo)

keyPoints: Anadolu Agency reported the Eiffel Tower was closed to visitors Thursday due to a nationwide strike in France.
Sortiraparis reported the strike and demonstration were also disrupting museums and monuments in Paris, with the Louvre limiting visitor access and the Palace of Versailles possibly closing.
Chinadaily reported demonstrations took place across French cities, and Mixvale reported that the strike paralyzed public transport.
The Meridian story does not yet have a union-by-union breakdown or official turnout figures from a wire service; those details are not verified here.
body:
France’s nationwide strike on Thursday, November 5, shut the Eiffel Tower to visitors and disrupted public transport, as unions and protesters took to the streets across the country.

## Paris landmarks

Anadolu Agency reported the Eiffel Tower was closed to visitors on Thursday because of the strike. Sortiraparis reported the tower remained closed, the Louvre was limiting visitor access, and the Palace of Versailles might close.

## Transport

Mixvale reported that the nationwide general strike called by the country’s unions paralyzed public transport. Sortiraparis, in headlines on its site, listed planned disruptions that included a strike affecting RER and Transilien rail services, 25 Paris metro stations closed on Thursday, and an airport strike at Roissy and Orly. Those were planned disruptions as reported by that outlet, not wire-confirmed totals.

## Protests across France

Chinadaily reported that demonstrations took place across the country on Thursday, with images from the day showing gendarmes deployed in France. Sortiraparis also carried a headline about a police-confirmed demonstration route in Paris for the same day. The reporting reviewed for this story does not yet give union-by-union demands, official turnout figures or an expected end date for the strike.

## What is not yet confirmed

Meridian has not verified turnout figures, the strike’s expected length or the closure time for the Eiffel Tower from an official operator notice. Meridian will update this story when a wire service or official source confirms those details.

## Why it matters for visitors

The Eiffel Tower closure and the Louvre’s limits fall on one of the busiest travel days of the week, when tourists rely on Paris’s major sites. Sortiraparis reported the Palace of Versailles might also close, so visitors planning trips to the region should check each venue’s official notice before going.

## Context

The reporting reviewed for this story describes the strike as a nationwide general strike called by the country’s unions. Meridian has not yet confirmed the specific grievances behind the walkout from a wire service or union statement, and will add them once verified.
